be brutal. just give me a plain list of edits to tighten the ending, no commentary

"By the time the tide pulls out, the boardwalk planks are slick and the egrets stand like they own the place. I have spent every November of my life counting them, and I have spent every other month trying to leave. This semester I lead the mechanical subteam on my robotics team, and today I spent two hours fixing a gearbox mount that would not stay true. Maybe that is what the marsh taught me: that things worth keeping need constant, patient adjustment, and that I am the kind of person who will keep adjusting them, wherever I end up, even if it is somewhere far away from here."

Here are the edits for the ending:

1. Cut "Maybe that is what the marsh taught me:" and start with "The marsh taught me that".
2. Replace "things worth keeping need constant, patient adjustment" with "what matters needs patient adjustment".
3. Delete "and that I am the kind of person who will keep adjusting them". Use "and I will keep adjusting".
4. Cut "even if it is somewhere far away from here". The earlier line about trying to leave already covers it.
5. Optional: end on an image. For example: "...wherever I end up, I will keep adjusting, the way the egrets return with each tide."
6. Trim "today I spent two hours fixing a gearbox mount that would not stay true" to "I spent two hours straightening a gearbox mount that would not stay true" so the tense matches the rest.

Tightened ending:

"The marsh taught me that what matters needs patient adjustment, and wherever I end up, I will keep adjusting, the way the egrets return with each tide."
